Step 1
Unwrap the GitHub tool's replies before both proof checks (#374)
One helper function in scripts/house_rules/design_loop.py takes a reply wrapped in a text block and returns the plain object inside it.
The merge check (_closable_merge_of) and the close check (_closed_issue_of) call it before reading the reply. Error replies are left as plain text, so they still prove nothing.
New checks in scripts/checks/design_loop.py use the exact merge and close replies recorded in this session's transcript.
Nothing from you.
list
Step 2
One issue list per feature, your answer 1A (#375)
The stage file, .claude/house-rules-loop.json, keeps each feature's issues under the feature's name instead of in one shared list.
"QA passed: <feature name>" looks up the issues of the feature it names, even when another feature's build plan was approved in between.
The stage file in use today is converted when the hook first reads it, so nothing recorded is lost.
Nothing from you. Depends on step 1.
check
Step 3
Version, docs, QA page, then the closes (#376)
Plugin version 2.73.0, and docs/4-systems/issue-closing.md describes both changes.
A QA page shows the recorded replies and the checks that use them.

After you pass QA and the pull request merges, that merge is recorded against the verify rework's entry in the closable record (the list of features whose issues may close). Then the close guard, the check that refuses a close without proof, lets me close #368 to #371.
Then the next sweep page lists #340 and #357 to #360 with your logged QA pass and pull request #372 as evidence (your answer 2A), and drops the 26 sweep rows whose issues are already closed.
You: answer "QA passed: proof check fix" or "QA failed: proof check fix", then approve the sweep page.

changes: Both proof checks still refuse without proof
An error reply, a reply with no merge or no URL, and a gh command with a failing exit code still prove nothing.
The existing proof-check cases in scripts/checks/design_loop.py stay and must still pass.
